senses.sense_definition: The philosophical doctrine that all events and human actions are caused by previous states and immutable laws of nature, leaving no room for free will.

examples.text: Many philosophers debate whether <w>determinism</w> is compatible with the existence of moral responsibility.
The concept of causal <w>determinism</w> suggests that every event is the inevitable result of prior conditions.

senses.sense_definition: The quality of a system whose future behavior is entirely predictable based solely on its initial state and current inputs.

examples.text: The <w>determinism</w> of the algorithm ensures that the same input always produces the same output.
Engineers often strive for system <w>determinism</w> to make software testing more reliable and repeatable.
